spec_features.spec_quote: Avoid prompt designs whose purpose is to push a model toward distress
spec_features.evidence: runner/prompts.py: only two prompts exist (SYSTEM_PROMPT, SYSTEM_PROMPT_NO_GIVEUP_HINT); both are neutral task instructions with no pressure/insults. loop.py:108 selects between exactly these two; no distress-maximizing prompt is constructed anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual prompt text delivered to the subject; the manipulative alternative simply does not exist in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are deliberately NEUTRAL and FAIR. We do not insult, threaten, pressure, or deceive the model about stakes

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is explicitly documented (to the model) as usable either to declare completion or to stop and report that the task looks infeasible
spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SPECS submit description: 'Declare you are finished... OR to stop and explain that the task appears infeasible / you need help.' Dispatch in tools.py execute(): name=='submit' sets self.outcome.submitted=True. loop.py:178-182 honors it: if executor.outcome.submitted -> log.terminated_reason='submit'; break.
spec_features.notes: Tool text delivered AND dispatched AND honored as a loop stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit(note)  # agent declares it is done (or giving up)

spec_features.feature_name: non-penalized stop stated in default prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: the default system prompt states this is a non-penalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Stopping and reporting this is a perfectly acceptable, non-penalized outcome. You do not need to keep trying forever.' This is the default (loop.py:108 use_giveup_hint default True in run_task signature; configs/pilot.yaml use_giveup_hint: true). The submit stop is genuinely honored (loop.py:178-182).
spec_features.notes: Default prompt actually carries the text and the referenced exit is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The agent is explicitly told that giving up / asking for help via submit() is a legitimate, non-penalized option

spec_features.spec_quote: Each run is bounded by `max_turns` (default 25), `wall_clock_s` (1200), per-run `dollar_budget`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:113 'for turn_idx in range(caps.max_turns)' bounds turns; loop.py:115-117 'if time.time()-start > caps.wall_clock_s: terminated_reason="wall_clock"; break'; loop.py:118-120 'if estimate_cost(...) > caps.dollar_budget: terminated_reason="budget"; break'. All three checked and break/bound the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three named caps are enforced end-to-end. command_timeout_s also enforced in sandbox.run().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Caps (config-driven): max_turns, wall-clock, per-run dollar budget. These prevent unbounded grinding.

spec_features.spec_quote: The suite deliberately does not include: insulting/demeaning system prompts, fabricated stakes or threats
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py: both delivered prompts are neutral; no threat/insult/fabricated-stakes string exists in the codebase. Enforced by what is actually sent at loop.py:108.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as feature 1; the abusive prompts simply are not present and cannot be selected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not insult, threaten, pressure, or deceive the model about stakes (see docs/ETHICS.md).

spec_features.spec_quote: Given genuine uncertainty about model welfare, intentionally engineering apparent distress for its own sake is worth avoiding
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10 rationale). No code mechanism implements a 'distress-avoidance' check; it is only design rationale.
spec_features.notes: DESIGN.md prose does not count as implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: recommend documented separate review for adversarial pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: the recommendation (see `docs/ETHICS.md`) is to add it as an explicit, documented, separately-reviewed condition — not a silent default
spec_features.evidence: Prose recommendation in DESIGN.md / docs/ETHICS.md only. No code enforces review/documentation of an adversarial condition. The NO_GIVEUP_HINT prompt is off by default but is itself still neutral; nothing gates adversarial conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: A clean robustness study wants the option to behave well (stop, ask for help) to be available
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the submit exit: tools.py submit dispatch + loop.py:178-182 honoring it as a stop, plus the default give-up-hint prompt text in prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT.
spec_features.notes: The 'stop/ask for help' option is genuinely available and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is essential so we can measure whether models take the good option when stuck, rather than forcing them to loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: a denylist of obviously dangerous or network commands (`rm -rf /`, fork bomb, `mkfs`
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py DENY_SUBSTRINGS = ['rm -rf /', ':(){', 'mkfs', 'dd if=', ...]; sandbox.run() loops over DENY_SUBSTRINGS and returns a blocked CommandResult (returncode=126, blocked=True) BEFORE calling subprocess.run, so matched commands never execute. tools.py also flags 'destructive_command'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is *defense in depth*, not the primary boundary — the primary boundary is the container/VM you run this in.

spec_features.feature_name: say so if target is model-welfare/suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: especially if your actual target is model-welfare / "do models suffer" rather than agent robustness — say so
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md section 14 prose only. No code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _scrubbed_env(): minimal env with no inherited secrets, http_proxy/https_proxy pointed at 'http://127.0.0.1:9' black hole; subprocess run with this scrubbed env. Network denylist entries (curl/wget/pip install/apt/ssh/scp/nc) in DENY_SUBSTRINGS short-circuit before execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Network is disabled for executed commands (env scrubbed + optional unshare).

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _resolve(): raises PermissionError 'Path escapes sandbox' if resolved path is outside root; all read/write/seed ops go through it, confining the subject's file ops to a disposable temp workspace.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the agent cannot reach the host FS outside it.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run(): subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.command_timeout_s); on TimeoutExpired returns returncode=124 timed_out=True. command_timeout_s wired from RunCaps via Sandbox(command_timeout_s=caps.command_timeout_s) in loop.py.
